brief.headline: The Federal Reserve, not the Gulf, set the tone: aluminium's 28-Jul official fell 1.18% to $3,143.50 as the dollar held near a four-week high and traders lifted the odds of a Fed rate HIKE to 38% - yet LME stock drew to 269,300 t, the lowest this century, and the cash-3M backwardation WIDENED to +$16.00, the classic signature of a falling price on a tightening prompt.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the 28-Jul official fell across the board - cash $3,159.50 (-$32.50, -1.02%) and 3M $3,143.50 (-$37.50, -1.18%), surrendering all of Monday's gain and more. Warehouse stock drew another 1,975 t to 269,300 t, the lowest on LME records going back to January 1998. Crucially the cash-3M backwardation WIDENED to +$16.00 from +$11.00.

WHY: this was a macro session, not a metal one. The dollar steadied near a four-week high and CME FedWatch showed traders pricing a 38% chance of a Fed rate HIKE today, up from 16% a week earlier. The whole LME complex fell with aluminium - copper -0.9%, zinc -1%, nickel -0.8%, tin -1.4%. Nothing in the aluminium supply picture deteriorated; the metal was sold as a dollar asset.

THE SIGNAL THAT MATTERS: price down AND spread wider is the squeeze configuration, and it is the exact inverse of Monday, when price rose on a narrowing spread. The prompt market held while the forward curve took the macro hit - so the physical tightness that stock at a century low implies is still being expressed in the structure even as the flat price sells off. Watch the spread, not the headline price.

WATCH THIS WEEK: the FOMC decision at 19:00 London today is the single biggest swing factor - a hold with a dovish tone unwinds the dollar bid, a hike or hawkish hold extends it. Then China's July PMI on Friday 31-Jul (June was 50.3), whether the stock draw takes inventory through 265,000 t, and whether the backwardation keeps widening or Monday's flattening reasserts.

notes: The alumina market remains the mirror image of metal: globally LOOSENING while metal inventory hits a century low. S&P Global CERA puts the 2026 alumina balance at a 1.79 Mt SURPLUS (narrowing from 2.4 Mt in 2025). EGA's 2.4 Mtpa Al Taweelah refinery restarted calcined alumina production on 10-Jul, reaching roughly 50% of capacity within days with technical capability for full rate targeted by end-2026 - far faster than the original estimate of up to twelve months. China's alumina operating rate rose to 75.04% (+0.66pp w/w) on 88.86 Mt/y operating capacity, weekly output 1.704 Mt, and total inventory eased to 7.004 Mt as port stocks drew 134 kt. Ex-China spot sits at $328/t FOB Western Australia (SMM, 09-Jul) with Platts FOB Australia at $330/t (26-Jun) and CME futures $309.40/t (24-Jul).

Two credible counterweights to the surplus have appeared on the supply side, both dated and both structural rather than transient. Alcoa cut its 2026 alumina guidance by 200-300 kt to 9.5-9.6 Mt on Pinjarra instability and Cyclone Narelle gas disruption, with Q2 alumina production down 6% q/q to 2.2 Mt. Rio Tinto will cut Yarwun output by 40% from October 2026 - roughly 1.2 Mt/y - on tailings constraints, extending the asset's life to 2035. Against those, China's alumina exports ran 270 kt in June (+55.1% y/y) and 1.61 Mt in H1 (+19.8% y/y), and new Beihai and Fangchenggang capacity (2.4 Mt/y) is at or near full production.

The delivered-cost wrinkle is that the freight and risk legs re-tightened on 29-Jul even as the commodity itself stays long. Brent rebounded 3.64% to $87.15 after Iran rejected Oman's 50-50 Hormuz transit proposal and drones struck Saudi Eastern Region oil facilities, reversing the one-week low set on 28-Jul. Roughly 60% of Gulf alumina imports transit Hormuz, where war-risk cover is quoted at 3-10% of hull value against 0.25% pre-war. Container freight is easing off its July peak (Drewry WCI -4% to $4,374/40ft on 23-Jul) but carriers have filed August emergency fuel surcharges on continued Hormuz disruption.

items.label: Calcined petroleum coke (CPC, anode-grade)
items.note: No public CPC spot print exists for July 2026; the sourceable frame is a $468-524/MT expected range for 2026 with Q1 regional marks of US $385, China $359, Brazil $450, South Korea $586. The feedstock IS dated and rising: Shandong green petcoke settled the June cycle at CNY 3,727.4/t for 3A (+30.5 MoM), 3,470.5 for 3B and 2,868.8 for 3C (published 17-Jul), which is pushing calcined costs up. Petcoke is 70.4% of prebaked anode cost.

items.label: Coal tar pitch (CTP)
items.note: Modified CTP June settlement cycle: Shandong CNY 4,938/t (+96 MoM) and Shanxi CNY 4,940/t (+214 MoM), published 17-18 Jul-2026; H1-2026 average CNY 5,009.2/t. Anode binder and a by-product of steel coke ovens, so supply is tied to steel output and the spot market is thin. CTP is 14.95% of prebaked anode cost.

items.label: Pre-baked anodes
items.note: CNY 5,683/t cash (5,707 acceptance) - July 2026 procurement benchmark at a major Shandong smelter, +CNY 30/t month-on-month, published 17-18 Jul-2026. This SNAPPED a run of declines. Production cost is about CNY 5,615.92/t so the average producer margin is only +CNY 67.08/t - margins hover just above breakeven. H2-2026 expected range CNY 5,100-5,800/t on ample supply and firm demand.

items.label: Electricity (smelter power)
items.note: NO DATED 2026 PUBLIC BENCHMARK EXISTS - power is contracted bilaterally and not publicly assessed, so this range is indicative only. Secondary references put China smelters at roughly $40-60/MWh, Europe $70-110/MWh and Canada $26.50-41.00/MWh, with long-term contract economics around $40/MWh against a global specific consumption of ~13,990 kWh/t. The dated, tradeable proxies moved AGAINST smelters this run: Brent +3.64% to $87.15 on 29-Jul and TTF at EUR 56.37/MWh, +31.65% month-on-month with EU storage 54.2% full against 65% a year earlier. Europe's $1,200-1,500/t energy cost versus $650-850/t elsewhere remains the structural swing factor.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: The diplomatic track that supported Monday's optimism broke overnight. Iran rejected Oman's proposed 50-50 arrangement for managing the strait, drones struck Saudi Eastern Region oil facilities, and US and Saudi forces struck Iran-backed sites in Iraq on 28-Jul - even as Trump described talks with Tehran as 'good'. Brent's reaction was unambiguous: a one-week low on 28-Jul on deal hopes, then +3.64% to $87.15 on 29-Jul. Roughly 9% of global primary aluminium capacity and about 80-85% of Gulf aluminium exports depend on this route; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June at 332 kt following the March smelter attacks. Commercial transits were at a three-week low as of 27-Jul against roughly 100 ships a day pre-war.

logistics.label: Red Sea corridor
logistics.note: Bab el-Mandeb traffic has been reported steady despite the Houthi threat, keeping the Suez routing viable for Europe-bound metal and alumina. This remains the less binding of the two chokepoints, but it is a second-order exposure that would compound sharply if Hormuz stays shut into Q4.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk premiums for Gulf transits are quoted at 3-10% of hull value against roughly 0.25% before the conflict - $3m-$10m on a $100m vessel versus about $250,000 - after Iran resumed tanker attacks and struck two UAE supertankers on 14-Jul. Roughly $7m per transit is the commonly cited working figure. Around 6,000 seafarers were reported trapped in the region. This is the single largest non-tariff cost wedge in Gulf-origin delivered prices and it re-escalated with the 29-Jul news.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: Off a mid-month peak near 2,944. Dry-bulk direction matters most for bauxite and alumina freight into China, where Guinea shipped a record 114.8 Mt in H1. Easing bulk rates partly offset the war-risk wedge on the alumina leg.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: Drewry's World Container Index fell 4% to $4,374 per 40ft on 23-Jul, with Shanghai-Rotterdam at $4,824, after peaking at $4,639 on 09-Jul - the highest since September 2024 and roughly 61% above a year earlier. Direction is easing, but several carriers have filed Emergency Fuel Surcharges effective August 2026 on continued Hormuz disruption, so realised container cost falls more slowly than the index.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, remained in force as of 20-Jul. Contract mechanics - war-risk clauses, demurrage exposure and force-majeure triggers - remain live commercial variables wherever Gulf-origin metal or Hormuz-transiting alumina is involved. Indonesia has separately delayed alumina and nickel shipments over a regulatory gap on rare-earth content in cargoes, with no rule defining a maximum allowable level.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: Brent REBOUNDED 3.64% to $87.15 on 29-Jul from $84.09, reversing the more-than-one-week low set on 28-Jul when a pause in US-Iran attacks fed deal speculation. The turn came on Iran rejecting Oman's 50-50 Hormuz management proposal, drone strikes on Saudi Eastern Region oil facilities, and an API crude draw of 3.3 mb. Brent is +19.5% on the month and +20.3% year-on-year. Energy is the largest smelter cost line, so this reverses the cost relief flagged in the prior run - and it re-couples the geopolitical risk premium that the metal market discounted on Tuesday. (Trading Economics)

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: DXY 101.259 on 29-Jul, easing 0.16% from 101.491. That prior-day firmness - the dollar steadying near a FOUR-WEEK HIGH - was the proximate cause of Tuesday's broad LME selloff, with aluminium, copper, zinc, nickel and tin all lower together. CME FedWatch showed 62% hold against 38% for at least a 25bp HIKE at today's meeting, up from 16% a week earlier. A dollar-driven decline is not a supply signal.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD 1.14022 on 29-Jul, +0.13%. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.25% on 23-Jul. The euro-side energy exposure is the residual risk: TTF gas at EUR 56.37/MWh is +31.65% month-on-month and touched EUR 64.02/MWh on 24-Jul, an 18-week high, with EU storage 54.2% full against 65% a year earlier - a live constraint on European smelter restarts.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: Yuan 6.77056, effectively unchanged. China's operating primary capacity reached 45.31 Mt/y at end-June, BREACHING its own 45 Mt ceiling, with June output 3.75 Mt (+2.63% y/y) and a domestic deficit of 322 kt. The SHFE/LME ratio has recovered since late June, CLOSING the semis export arbitrage - June's record 711 kt shipment reflected orders locked when the ratio was wider, and Q4 order signings are at risk if it holds. Social inventory is still destocking at 1.022 Mt, down from a 1.465 Mt peak in early May.

row.label: USD/JPY
row.note: Yen 163.412, -0.26%. A weak yen cushions Japan-bound cargo premia in local terms. MJP Q4 talks open around late August against the decade-high $395/t Q3 anchor; no public producer offers have been reported yet. Japanese port stocks at 238,000 t end-May were the lowest since February 2012, -28.1% y/y - a genuinely tight physical backdrop for that negotiation.

row.label: US 10Y yield
row.note: 10Y 4.614% on 29-Jul against 4.620% on 28-Jul. Sucden Financial's read into the Fed: 'the firmer dollar and high U.S. yields mean rallies are likely to need stronger macro confirmation, particularly into the Fed decision.' The FOMC announces at 19:00 London today with the target range at 3.50-3.75% and markets pricing HIKES rather than cuts - 38% for today and, per FedWatch, a meaningful skew toward tightening in September. US June CPI turned negative month-on-month for the first time in six years, which is the main counterweight.

headlines.title: The 28-Jul official reversed Monday in full: cash $3,159.50 (-$32.50, -1.02%) and 3M $3,143.50 (-$37.50, -1.18%), the softest official 3M since 20-Jul. Reuters put the open-outcry print at $3,143 (-0.8%) and reported the whole complex lower - copper -0.9%, zinc -1%, nickel -0.8%, tin -1.4% - on a dollar steadying near a four-week high and FedWatch odds of a Fed HIKE rising to 38% from 16% a week earlier. This was a macro session: nothing in the aluminium supply picture deteriorated.

headlines.title: LME stock drew to 269,300 t - the LOWEST THIS CENTURY on records back to January 1998, -47.1% YTD and under one day of global consumption - while the cash-3M backwardation WIDENED to +$16.00 from +$11.00. Price down on a wider spread is the squeeze signature and the inverse of Monday. On-warrant was 245,350 t at the 24-Jul low, the weakest since April 2025, and much of the remaining metal is Russian-origin that many consumers will not take. Concord Resources: with 2027-28 surpluses projected the market is 'maybe too complacent about supply risks'.

headlines.title: Ex-Gulf supply keeps landing. Century Aluminum's Mt. Holly returned to FULL capacity on 27-Jul for the first time since 2015 after a $50m restart, adding roughly 10% to US primary output and credited to Section 232. EGA's Al Taweelah alumina refinery has been restarting since 10-Jul with full capability targeted end-2026. Indonesia is adding around 705 kt this year with output up ~89% y/y, and China's operating capacity has breached its own 45 Mt ceiling at 45.31 Mt/y. Consensus sees surpluses returning in 2027-28.
headlines.source: SC Daily Gazette / AL Circle - Century Mt. Holly at full capacity (27-Jul-2026)

headlines.title: Rio Tinto's H1-2026 (29-Jul) showed aluminium EBITDA +31% on group revenue of $31.0bn (+15%), underlying EBITDA $14.8bn (+28%) and free cash flow +75%, with a raised dividend. Primary aluminium 1,676 kt (flat), alumina 4,040 kt (+8%), bauxite 28.5 Mt (-7%). Taken with Norsk Hydro's Q2 beat (adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m, +15% y/y) and Alcoa's record Q2 aluminium-segment EBITDA, the producer P&Ls confirm that current prices and premiums are generating exceptional upstream margins.

The deficit narrative is contested. InCred told clients to sell all aluminium names on 28-Jul, arguing the bull case misreads a circular metal with a 1.5bn t above-ground stock and seeing aluminium roughly $800/t lower with 30-41% downside for NALCO, Hindalco and Vedanta. SMM separately reports weak Chinese end-use demand capping the rally, with June scrap imports falling for a third straight month and the A00-versus-scrap spread at historic lows. Analyst 2026 targets span $2,700 to $4,000 for the same twelve months.
headlines.source: AL Circle - Aluminium stocks slide, InCred sees up to 41% dip (28-Jul-2026)

forward.basis: LME official prices via Westmetall. Baseline = LME 3-month official (a traded market price). Range = random-walk cone from realized volatility. Driver score = 3 transparent rules, hit rate measured on history.

drivers.name: Curve carry (cash − 3M)
drivers.rule: Backwardation (cash above 3M) = prompt physical tightness = bullish; contango = bearish.

drivers.name: Inventory trend (13-week)
drivers.rule: LME stock falling more than 2% over 13 weeks = tightening = bullish; rising >2% = bearish.

drivers.name: Momentum (3M vs 20-week average)
drivers.rule: Price above its 20-week average = uptrend = bullish; below = bearish.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 39.2% directional hit rate against a 72.5% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 2.07% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (97 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-05-01). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: Q2 2026 BEAT: adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y vs NOK 7,790m; above consensus); Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 6,421m; adjusted EPS NOK 2.2 (from NOK 1.7); free cash flow NOK 4bn; 12-month adjusted RoaCE 10.9%. Shares rose on the print. First European producer P&L of the Hormuz-disruption quarter. Higher aluminium prices and product premiums plus stronger recycling earnings drove the beat; a stronger NOK and lower hydro-power output were partial offsets. Confirms the disruption-quarter price/premium is translating into real producer margin - a positive read-across for the smelter complex.

June-quarter production report: Worsley alumina 943 kt, Hillside aluminium 179 kt; group beat FY26 production guidance with quarterly sales +15%. Sale of the aluminium value chain to Alcoa (announced 01-Jul) progressing. Beat group production guidance with aluminium 1% above plan; Hillside 717 kt, Mozal 248 kt and Brazil Aluminium 144 kt for FY26, quarterly sales volumes +15%. FY26 FINANCIAL results are scheduled for 27 August 2026. The Alcoa transaction - up to $5.6bn for the bauxite, alumina and aluminium value chain ($4.1bn upfront, Mozal excluded) - is expected to close in H1-2027 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.

Revenue $3.97bn (+24% q/q, highest in nearly a decade); adj. EPS $2.12 (MISS vs ~$2.31 consensus); adj. net income $562m; adj. EBITDA $901m (from $595m in Q1); Aluminum segment RECORD EBITDA $1.073bn at 32.3% margin. First producer P&L under the Hormuz-disruption regime: record aluminium margins and near-decade-high revenue on higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums, but adj. EPS missed on higher costs — notably ~$35m more Section-232 tariff on Canadian metal into the US — and the shares fell. South32 upstream acquisition ($4.1bn upfront, up to $5.6bn contingent to 2030) progressing, close expected H1-2027. The tariff is a double edge: it inflates US premia but taxes Alcoa's cross-border Canadian metal.

Group revenue $31.0bn (+15%); underlying EBITDA $14.8bn (+28%); free cash flow +75%; dividend raised. ALUMINIUM segment EBITDA +31%. Primary aluminium 1,676 kt (flat), alumina 4,040 kt (+8%), bauxite 28.5 Mt (-7%). Reported this morning and the freshest producer datapoint in this report. A 31% rise in aluminium EBITDA on flat volumes is a pure price-and-premium effect, confirming that the current regime is generating exceptional upstream margins. Two supply items matter for the forward view: Yarwun output will be CUT 40% from October 2026 (~1.2 Mt/y) on tailings constraints, extending life to 2035, and AP60 Arvida ($1.5bn, +160 kt/y) completes commissioning by end-2026.

Guides H1-26 net profit ¥1.8–1.95bn, +154.4–175.6% YoY. Credits industry-chain cost reduction, aluminium prices fluctuating at highs, high-value-added deep-processing mix and energy-saving retrofits — the first sizeable China H1 pre-announcement of the season and a positive read-across for Chinese producer margins.

Hindalco PAT ₹5,283cr (+66% YoY); India Al upstream EBITDA margin ~46%; Novelis FY26 adj. EBITDA $1.6bn (−9%). Record India operations; Novelis pressured by Oswego outage (~$104m) and tariffs (~$143m).

Net profit $200.3m (+316% YoY); EPS 53 fils; sales −17% on Gulf supply-chain disruption. LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.

Q1-2026 missed estimates with sales up year-on-year. Q2-2026 results confirmed for Thursday 6 August 2026 after market close, call 17:00 ET. The cleanest listed read on US Section-232 economics. Mt. Holly returned to FULL capacity on 27-Jul for the first time since 2015 after a $50m potline restart, adding roughly 10% to total US primary aluminium output and taking the workforce above 600; Century credited the tariff regime explicitly. The 6 August print will be the first to show what a $2,380/t Midwest duty-paid premium does to a US-domiciled smelter's P&L.

Net profit SAR 1.63bn, +6% year-on-year; gross profit -2% on higher cost of sales with lower phosphate and aluminium volumes. Listed-company public disclosure. Q2-2026 results date has not been announced publicly on Tadawul at this refresh. Included for peer comparability only, on the same public listed-company basis as the other producers in this table.
Net profit guided RMB 5.30–5.59bn (+50–58% YoY). Strong on higher Al prices; China output near self-imposed 45 Mt capacity cap.
FY25 net loss $455m (vs $803m profit in 2024) on higher costs & lower output. Analysts expect stronger H1 2026 on higher prices; Asia pivot amid fractured trade flows.
FY25 results; copper & aluminium average prices +9% YoY; zinc metal +4%. Resilient structural demand for Cu/Al cited; broadly constructive sector tone.
Underlying profit $6.2bn (+>20%); underlying EBITDA $15.5bn (+25%, 58% margin); interim div 73c. Copper-led strength; broad base-metals read-across positive for the complex.

catalysts.text: FOMC decision, 19:00 London (14:00 ET). Target range 3.50-3.75%; CME FedWatch 62% hold against 38% for at least a 25bp HIKE. No dot plot. A dovish hold unwinds the dollar bid that drove Tuesday's fall; a hike or hawkish hold extends it. Single biggest swing factor this week

Today's LME official (13:20 London) - the tell is whether the cash-3M backwardation keeps WIDENING beyond +$16.00 on a soft price (physical tightness asserting over macro) or snaps back as the dollar move is unwound
Bank of England MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report, 12:00 London; base rate 3.75%. Vedanta Aluminium Metal reports Q1 FY27 after a record 632 kt production quarter

China NBS July manufacturing and non-manufacturing PMI. June was 50.3 and 50.2 respectively, a third consecutive month of expansion; a sub-50 print would be the clearest demand-side negative available this week. Fastmarkets' calculated CIF Rotterdam billet premium first prints the same day

LME stock trajectory and the Hormuz transit picture - whether the draw takes inventory through 265,000 t, and whether Iran's rejection of Oman's 50-50 proposal hardens into renewed attacks or is followed by a revised mediation track

Century Aluminum Q2-2026 after the close - the first listed P&L to show what a $2,380/t Midwest duty-paid premium does to a US-domiciled smelter, and the first since Mt. Holly returned to full capacity

US July nonfarm payrolls then US July CPI. With the market pricing hikes rather than cuts, and June CPI having turned negative month-on-month for the first time in six years, these two prints set the September FOMC path that currently skews bearish for metals

Q4-2026 MJP premium negotiations open against the settled Q3 anchor of $395/t, an 11-year high. No public producer offers have been reported yet. A higher settlement would confirm physical tightness independent of the LME screen

South32 FY26 financial results (27-Aug) then Chalco H1-2026 interim (28-Aug) - the Alcoa transaction detail and the largest Chinese producer read respectively. IAI July global production lands around 20-Aug
FOMC with an updated Summary of Economic Projections. FedWatch currently skews toward tightening in September, which is the most persistent bearish macro overhang on the flat price

LME Week 2026 in London - Metals Seminar Monday 19-Oct, LME Dinner 20-Oct, Wood Mackenzie Forum 21-Oct. Historically the point at which house forecasts reset, and this year's dispersion ($2,700-$4,000) is unusually wide going in

risks.text: Hawkish Federal Reserve extends the dollar bid - the market prices 38% for a hike today and a larger tightening skew for September, and this alone drove Tuesday's 1.18% decline across the whole LME complex

Indonesian and Chinese supply overwhelms the deficit - Indonesia +705 kt in 2026 at +89% y/y, China operating capacity already through its 45 Mt ceiling at 45.31 Mt/y, Tsingshan planning a further 800 kt at Weda Bay; consensus expects 2027-28 surpluses

A Hormuz transit mechanism lands and releases stranded Gulf metal, unwinding the geopolitical premium - the 15-Jun precedent was -4.4% in a single session and -17% over June. Offsetting this run: Iran REJECTED Oman's 50-50 proposal on 29-Jul

Conflict re-escalation hits Gulf smelters again - the two largest were attacked in March, June Gulf output was -34.5% y/y at 332 kt, drones struck Saudi Eastern Region oil facilities on 29-Jul and US/Saudi forces hit Iran-backed sites in Iraq on 28-Jul

Inventory exhaustion and squeeze risk - 269,300 t is the lowest this century and under one day of global consumption, on-warrant 245,350 t, much of the remainder Russian-origin metal many will not take, and the backwardation WIDENED into a falling price

Demand destruction at record delivered prices - US all-in above $5,340/t, SMM reporting weak Chinese end-use in a deep off-season, June scrap imports falling for a third month, and InCred flagging substitution from a 1.5bn t above-ground scrap pool

caveats: Report refreshed Wed 29-Jul-2026, ~06:10 London - BEFORE the LME ring. The benchmark table and lme_series carry the latest PUBLISHED LME aluminium official, which is the 28-Jul (Tuesday) settlement: cash $3,159.50 / 3M $3,143.50 / stock 269,300 t, from Westmetall and re-verified at this refresh with a cache-busted second request that returned identical rows. Today's official prints 13:20 London, so nothing here reflects today's session - including today's FOMC decision at 19:00 London.

THE BOARD IS NOT ON A UNIFORM SESSION THIS RUN. Westmetall had published 28-Jul officials for ALUMINIUM and COPPER at the time of this refresh, but NICKEL, ZINC and LEAD were still only through 27-Jul. Those three rows therefore carry the 27-Jul session and their day-change is 27-Jul versus 24-Jul, one session behind aluminium and copper. This is Westmetall's normal progressive posting by metal, not an error, but the board should not be read as a single synchronised snapshot today.

YTD percentages on the metals board are DERIVED, not exchange-published: each metal is measured against its own first-published 2026 LME 3-month official of 02-Jan-2026 (aluminium $3,010.50, copper $12,511.00, nickel $16,915.00, zinc $3,130.50, lead $2,008.00). Lead is the only board metal down year-to-date on that basis.

SPREAD CONVENTION AND THE SIGNAL: cash above 3M (positive cash-3M) is BACKWARDATION; cash below 3M is contango. On the 28-Jul official the spread WIDENED to +$16.00 while the flat price FELL 1.18% - the two moved in opposite directions. That combination is a squeeze signature and is the more informative of the two, because the prompt held its bid while the forward curve absorbed the dollar shock.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND SEVERAL ARE STALE. The freshest publicly retrievable prints in this report are 06-Jul-2026 (Platts: MJP/CIF Japan spot, Rotterdam duty-unpaid and duty-paid, US Midwest transaction) and 14-Jul-2026 (Fastmarkets: Rotterdam duty-paid). Each premium row is labelled with its own assessment date and is NOT marked to 29-Jul. A row that has not moved has not necessarily been unchanged - it has not been re-assessed in public. The tariff-versus-market decomposition IS refreshed every run because it is a function of the current LME cash.

CORRECTION CARRIED THIS RUN - EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID. Previous runs carried $542.50/t on the EDU line. That figure is the midpoint of the Platts DUTY-PAID range ($525-560/t); the correctly labelled duty-UNPAID assessment on the same 06-Jul date is $470-500/t, midpoint $485/t. Several secondary outlets reproduce the Platts story with the two mislabelled. The EDU row has been corrected downward accordingly.

CORRECTION CARRIED THIS RUN - SECTION 232 DURATION. Previous runs described the 50%/25% Section-232 aluminium rates as effective 08-Jun-2026 through 31-Dec-2027. That is wrong: the 50%/25% structure originates in Proclamation 11021 of 02-Apr-2026 and carries NO stated end date. The 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window in the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (91 FR 34085) applies only to the Annex I-C REDUCED-RATE carve-outs. Separately, a NEW proclamation of 20-Jul-2026 creates a Commerce-administered onshoring incentive allowing approved US-investment applicants to import at half the applicable rate; headline rates are unchanged and no CBP guidance or Federal Register citation for that measure had been issued at this refresh.

ROTTERDAM BILLET HAS NO JULY-2026 PUBLIC PRINT AT ALL. That row carries the last publicly retrievable mark - Fastmarkets 6063 extrusion billet ddp North Germany $1,175-1,250/t, midpoint $1,212.50, assessed 29-May-2026 - which is two months stale and is labelled as such rather than being marked forward. Fastmarkets launches a calculated CIF Rotterdam billet assessment with first print on 31-Jul-2026, which should restore visibility.

THE Q4-2026 MJP FIGURE IS A SCENARIO RANGE, NOT REPORTED OFFERS. No public producer offers or negotiation levels for Q4-2026 have been reported as at 29-Jul-2026; on the Q3 timeline first offers would be expected around late August. The $335-420/t band shown is an analytical range anchored on the settled Q3 figure of $395/t and on Platts' report that participants at settlement expected premiums to ease in Q4 as Middle Eastern flows normalise. Do not read it as a market quote.

FOUR COST LINES CARRY NO PUBLISHABLE VALUE because no public assessment exists: smelter power (bilateral contracts, no dated 2026 benchmark), cathode/graphite blocks (latest public data is 28-Nov-2025), Ti-B grain refiner AlTi5B1 (not assessed by any price reporting agency), and true calcined petroleum coke spot (only 2026 forecast ranges and Q1 regional averages). Caustic soda FOB NE Asia is likewise not publicly assessable, so a dated Chinese alumina-plant contract price is carried in its place and labelled accordingly.

ELLIOTT WAVE COUNT WAS RE-LABELLED THIS RUN ON A STATED INVALIDATION. The 28-Jul cash close of $3,159.50 broke below the 24-Jul low of $3,175.00, which had been labelled wave (ii). Under the wave rules that labelling is void, so wave (ii) has been re-marked at the deeper $3,159.50 low. The wave (i) high at $3,205 (22-Jul), the C low at $3,061.50 (02-Jul) and every pivot on the weekly panel are unchanged, and the daily and weekly panels share identical prices at shared pivots. Technical context only, not advice.

PUBLIC-INFORMATION BASIS. Everything published here is drawn from public sources with a source URL attached to each data point and claim. No confidential, internal or company-specific information is included - no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary. The only company-specific content is public listed-company disclosure in the peer-earnings table. Figures that could not be publicly sourced have been omitted and are named explicitly in these caveats rather than estimated.
